items.label: diagnosis
items.evidence: numpy void scalars are not hashable, which means that a class with a np.void attribute cannot be hashed by `lru_cache`, which is used by the sharding codec class
items.rationale: Identifies root cause (unhashable np.void in lru_cache-used spec) and location in sharding codec, which the fix re-enables. No fix described.
items.author: d-v-b

items.label: fix_sketch
items.evidence: add another function that parses the inputs to `_get_chunk_spec` prior to calling it? This parser could then check for a void scalar, convert it to something hashable (e.g. `(dtype signature, raw bytes)`
items.rationale: Proposes converting void to raw bytes, similar in idea, but placed in sharding wrapper around _get_chunk_spec rather than ArraySpec hash/eq. Points somewhere the reference did not go, though bytes idea overlaps.
items.author: nenb

items.label: symptom
items.evidence: Also ran across this when trying to do sharding on arrays with structured dtypes (as they have np.void type fill values)
items.rationale: Reports the same failure with structured dtypes; no fix info.
items.author: sehoffmann
items.role: future fixer (author of the reference PR)

items.label: fix_sketch
items.evidence: the issue is the default `ArraySpec.__hash__` implementation which hashes each field, including `np.void` fill values. I think this can be fixed locally in `ArraySpec` by manually hashing `np.void` fill values based on their byte content (`.tobytes()`)
items.rationale: Describes the reference fix: custom ArraySpec hash using fill_value.tobytes().
items.author: sehoffmann
